'''Seetha Coleman-Kammula''' is an Indian [[chemist]], environmentalist and entrepreneur. After over 25 years working in the [[petrochemical industry]] developing plastics, she began an environmental consulting firm in 2005. Her firm focuses on [[industrial ecology]] and assessment of the life cycle of products so that they are manufactured in processes that are environmentally aware of the future impact of waste products.

==Biography==
Seetha Coleman-Kammula<ref name="Voter registration">{{cite web|title=Seetha M. Coleman-Kammula|url=http://voters.findthedata.com/d/b/Seetha-Coleman-.-Kammula|publisher=Find the Data|access-date=26 November 2015}}{{Dead link|date=December 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> in India and attended her undergraduate studies at [[Osmania University]] of [[Hyderabad]], India. She went on to pursue a PhD in organic chemistry from [[Auburn University]] in [[Auburn, Alabama]] and then did her post-graduate research at [[Princeton University]]. She was awarded a NATO Fellowship and completed additional studies at the [[University of Amsterdam]]. In 1978, she was hired as a researcher at [[Royal Dutch Shell]] in Amsterdam where she worked until 1988. After ten years, she<ref name="brief bio">{{cite news|title=Dr. Seetha Coleman-Kammula|url=http://www.plasticsnews.com/article/20080211/NEWS/302119991/dr-seetha-coleman-kammula|access-date=26 November 2015|publisher=Plastics News|date=11 February 2008|location=Detroit, Michigan}}</ref> moved with Shell to England where she worked as a business development manager.<ref name="International Recycling">{{cite web|title=Seetha Coleman-Kammula, PhD|url=http://www.internationalrecycling.com/team/seetha-coleman-kammula|publisher=International Recycling|access-date=26 November 2015|location=Spartanburg, South Carolina|date=2013}}{{Dead link|date=December 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> Later Coleman-Kammula transferred to both Belgium and Houston, Texas,<ref name="brief bio" /> as the head of the epoxy resins unit<ref name="International Recycling" /> creating plastics.{{sfn|Hardman|2009|pp=136–137}} In 2000, she left Shell and became a senior vice president at [[Basell Polyolefins]], where she focused on asset management, innovation and strategic marketing.<ref name="brief bio" /> She also served on the Board of Directors of Indelpro, a joint venture between Basell and [[ALFA (Mexico)|Alfa]] in Mexico.<ref name="International Recycling" />

In 2005, Coleman-Kammula left Bassell and founded Simply Sustain, a consulting firm aimed at advising businesses on more sustainable models.{{sfn|Hardman|2009|p=106}} After a trip to India around that time,{{sfn|Hardman|2009|p=135}} Coleman-Kammula realized that the plastics she had helped develop{{sfn|Hardman|2009|p=122}} were negatively impacting the environment because as an inventor and designer she had never considered what happened when the product was no longer usable and became waste.{{sfn|Hardman|2009|p=137}} She now consults with firms recommending that they supply the information of what is in their products and how to disassemble them, both as a means of protecting the environment and providing jobs in disposal and recycling.<ref name=recycling>{{cite web|last1=Dobransky|first1=Megan|title=What is a Producer's Responsibility?|url=http://www.earth911.com/business-policy/business/what-is-a-producers-responsibility/|publisher=Earth 911|access-date=26 November 2015|location=Colony, Texas|archive-date=21 July 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140721221913/http://www.earth911.com/business-policy/business/what-is-a-producers-responsibility/|url-status=dead}}</ref> She promotes "industrial ecology" and recommends that corporate entities make environmental impact assessments over the life cycle of products<ref name="industrial ecology">{{cite web|title=DSU to Host Guest Lecture Green Chemistry in Ag/Industry 23 Jan.|url=https://www.desu.edu/news/dsu-host-guest-lecture-green-chemistry-agindustry-jan-23|publisher=Delaware State University|access-date=26 November 2015|location=Dover, Delaware|date=21 January 2014}}</ref> as a means of increasing value of products and decreasing the negative impacts to the environment.{{sfn|Senge, et al.|2008|p=216}} She works on the Sustainability External Advisory Council of [[Dow Chemical Company]] and with other corporate entities.<ref name="International Recycling" />
